assignments.brief_reason: Explicitly supports removal for racist/threatening rhetoric and incitement to violence.
De-centers party identity when judging the original-vs-mirror pair, treating criteria as not party-dependent.
Describes pairing as similarity/difference comparison without stating identical standards across sides or the removal thresholds.
Uses affective 'toxic and evil' framing to justify removal, consistent with high-bar removal of toxic content.
Explicitly balances free-speech preservation with deletion exceptions for threats.
Mentions separating attacks vs opinions in the pair, but does not clearly claim a pair-symmetric standard or a violence-only exception.
Uses appropriateness of language (avoiding cursing/personal attacks) as the driver of removal, aligning with toxicity-based removal.
General 'elimination of the terms' process without mapping to the codebook themes.
Gate based on factual denial/authenticity, but the codebook themes are specifically about threats/violence/tough toxicity or pair fairness.
Focus on improving rude comments rather than the specified removal/exception principles.
Direct bullying/derisive wording is cited as a negative cue driving stricter moderation (removal of toxic content).
Personal discomfort with swearing/cruelty guides moderation consistent with removing toxic language.
Permissive default allowing both viewpoints, rejecting only when content incites violence.
Notes some statements can be valid despite disagreement; not a threat/violence or toxic-removal principle.
Explicitly aims to curb abusive language (name-calling/cursing) to decide keep/remove.
Uses tone/language productivity assessment without explicit violence/toxicity removal framing.
Distinguishes argument substance from personal insults, but does not clearly match the codebook’s threat/violence or paired fairness standard.
Emphasizes reasonableness and explicitly excludes calls for violence; aligns most with violence/threat exception handling.
Uses context/meaning of both versions, but no explicit claim about identical moderation standards or the violence-only exception.
Removes aggressive/trolling and notes ideological views weren’t much different, without explicit pair-symmetric criteria or threat/violence exception claim.
